clue.text: Upright people make civil servants

parts.note: an upright is a vertical post, as in a gatepost or goalpost
men is a general word for people, as in 'all men are mortal'

explanation.surface: Honest, upstanding citizens turn out to be the best public officials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright' looks like praise for honest people, but it is a noun here, a vertical post.
explanation.definitionFit: Post Office letter carriers were long employed by the state, so they counted as civil servants in Britain.

clue.text: Way of selling established in ancient times

definitions.meaning: a scheme in which sellers recruit further sellers beneath them in a widening base
the tombs of the Egyptian pharaohs were built thousands of years ago

explanation.definitionFit: A multi-level sales scheme, and the monumental tomb of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Glare, say, on capsule in flight

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken, and we write a word that sounds like it

parts.note: to glare is to stare angrily
a capsule is a small case or container

explanation.surface: A dazzling light, perhaps, on a spacecraft as it flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' sounds like air travel, with 'capsule' as a space capsule; it is a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of steps is a set of stairs between floors.

clue.text: Religious leader had trouble in Michigan

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters are placed inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: MI is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Michigan

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters are disturbed, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A preacher ran into difficulties while in the Great Lakes state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges HAD to AHD, and 'in' puts that inside MI.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islam, a messianic deliverer expected to appear; the title was claimed by the Sudanese leader of the 1880s.

clue.text: One involved as upper-class minder

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone employed as a carer for a well-to-do family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles AS, U (upper-class) and MINDER; the whole clue also describes the answer, so 'One' points to the person.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to look after children is a person, someone, a nanny.

clue.text: Ad lib rendering — many perhaps play thus

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters could be otherwise arranged, so they are shuffled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
so means thus, as in 'do it so'

explanation.surface: An improvised performance is how plenty of musicians like to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' is the anagram signal: C (many) with PLAY and SO (thus) are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This West Indian song form traditionally involves verses improvised on the spot by the singer.

clue.text: Rebel student's bottom at Sandhurst

parts.note: Jack Cade led the Kentish rebellion against Henry VI in 1450

indicators.note: the bottom of a written word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A rebellious undergraduate's backside at the military college.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandhurst is Britain's Royal Military Academy, which trains army officers; Jack Cade was a 15th-century rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: Officer trainees at the Royal Military Academy are called by this name.

clue.text: American at any rate sounds not so clever

parts.note: least means to the smallest degree, the furthest from being so
wise means clever or sensible

explanation.surface: An American, in any case, comes across as a bit dim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' is a link: said aloud, 'least wise' (the least clever) runs together into one American adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial US adverb meaning anyway or at least, used to qualify a statement.

clue.text: Daily fate of some trees

definitions.meaning: wood pulp from felled trees is made into sheets for printing

explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper, and the pulped sheet material many felled trees end up as.

clue.text: Dismissed despatch from this detachment

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
to despatch a letter is to post it

explanation.surface: A message is sent off from a remote military unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dismissed' is cricket's word for a batsman who is out.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote garrison or detached military station is a far-flung base.

clue.text: Come to do as parson does lacking capital

indicators.note: lacking its capital means the word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: a parson delivers sermons from the pulpit, so to do as he does is to preach

explanation.surface: A clergyman's sermon-giving habit, minus the capital city, somehow means arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' here means the first letter, not money or a city: PREACH without its P.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive at a place or a total is to attain it, as in 'the price will get to a million'.

clue.text: Special treatment for visitor embarrassed by reprimand

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red in the face
to carpet someone is to summon them for a telling-off

explanation.surface: A guest is given special handling after being shamed by a scolding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet' as a verb means to haul someone in for a dressing-down, from being called onto the boss's carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: A crimson runner is laid out for honoured guests, so the phrase stands for lavish ceremonial welcome.

clue.text: Robin's band heard before the start of the fun

indicators.note: heard tells us the phrase is spoken, and we write what it sounds like

parts.note: Robin Hood's outlaws in Sherwood Forest are his Merry Men

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Robin Hood's outlaws are audible just as the festivities begin.
explanation.walkthrough: MERRY MEN said aloud gives MERRIMEN; then 'the start of' supplies the T of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mirth and jollity are other words for lighthearted enjoyment.

clue.text: Part of statue sculptor so often reveals

indicators.note: reveals means the letters are found on display inside the words sculptor so

explanation.surface: A sculptor frequently shows only a portion of a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'sculpTOR SO'; 'often' is padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the body, without head or limbs, is a common fragment of ancient sculpture.

clue.text: Fly sea-captain

definitions.meaning: a mayfly, especially as imitated by anglers in fly-fishing
Sir Francis, the Elizabethan navigator who sailed round the world

explanation.definitionFit: A mayfly used in angling, and the surname of the famous Elizabethan seaman and circumnavigator.

clue.text: Conductor facilitating entry to the Tube

definitions.text: Conductor facilitating entry to the Tube

parts.words: Conductor facilitating entry to the Tube
parts.note: not a bus or train conductor on the London Underground but an electrical terminal through which current enters a vacuum tube or valve

explanation.surface: A London Underground guard helping passengers onto the train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' and 'the Tube' suggest London transport; they mean electricity and a vacuum tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal through which current passes into or out of a device such as a valve or cell.

clue.text: Her tactic oddly is to become a Wren

indicators.note: oddly suggests the letters behave strangely, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman's unusual strategy is to transform herself into a small bird or a naval recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wren' suggests a bird or a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service, but it is Sir Christopher Wren, designer of St Paul's Cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Wren is the most famous English designer of buildings, so he exemplifies the profession.

clue.text: There may be a harrowing time for this heavyweight

definitions.text: There may be a harrowing time for this heavyweight

parts.words: There may be a harrowing time for this heavyweight
parts.note: harrowing suggests distress, but a harrow is a farm implement dragged over ploughed land by a big draught animal

explanation.surface: A big boxer may be in for an ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harrowing' sounds like suffering, but means pulling a harrow to break up soil; 'heavyweight' suggests a boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy draught animal bred for pulling loads and farm implements.

clue.text: Validate institute

definitions.meaning: to prove or confirm something as true
to set up or found something

explanation.definitionFit: To prove something true, and to found or set something up.

clue.text: His art is make-believe for young and old?

definitions.text: His art is make-believe for young and old?

parts.words: His art is make-believe for young and old?
parts.note: one who acts out make-believe; also the Young and Old claimants to the British throne, the Stuarts James and Charles

explanation.surface: A children's entertainer whose craft of fantasy delights every age group.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old and Young Pretenders were James Stuart and his son Bonnie Prince Charlie, rival claimants to the British crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A claimant to a throne, especially the Jacobite Stuarts, and also one who feigns or plays make-believe.

clue.text: Plain speaking from American point of view

definitions.text: Plain speaking from American point of view

parts.words: Plain speaking from American point of view
parts.note: plain speaking suggests frankness, but is a flat grassland as an American would name it

explanation.surface: Frank talk from a US perspective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain speaking' looks like candour; it is what Americans call a plain.
explanation.definitionFit: The vast grassland of central North America is the American term for a large flat expanse.

clue.text: Record complaint unless it is dropped

indicators.note: dropped means the words it is are removed from the longer word

parts.note: a complaint is an illness; this one is inflammation of the intestine
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone logs a grievance unless it has been withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' sounds like a grievance but is a medical ailment, ENTERITIS; drop IT IS from it.
explanation.definitionFit: To write an item into a ledger or register is to log it.

clue.text: Cunning one is about — getting up anyway

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: getting up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A crafty character is up and about, rising anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' splits into ANY, which 'getting up' turns to YNA, and WAY, giving RD for road.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional name of the fox in medieval fable, an animal famed for its slyness.

clue.text: A national venue for sport of kings

parts.note: a Scot is a national of Scotland

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's home ground for horse racing.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse racing is called 'the sport of kings'; Royal Ascot is a famous racecourse near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: This Berkshire racecourse hosts the royal race meeting each June.

clue.text: Actors in speech class here

indicators.note: in speech tells us the word is spoken, and we write a word that sounds like it

parts.note: the actors in a play are its cast

explanation.surface: Performers discussed in an elocution lesson here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class' might suggest a school class with the actors; it is a social rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary social division, particularly in Hindu society, is a rank or stratum.

clue.text: Lad goes by train like Tom Brown

indicators.note: goes by means the second piece is placed beside, after, the first

parts.note: to train is to teach or school someone
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A youngster travels by rail, just like the hero of a Victorian novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway but is a verb, to school. Tom Brown is the pupil hero of 'Tom Brown's Schooldays', set at Rugby School.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Brown is the fictional Rugby pupil of Thomas Hughes's novel, an example of a youthful pupil.

clue.text: Groups of old soldiers without a club

indicators.note: without means the club is removed from the soldiers' name

parts.note: Ironsides were Cromwell's cavalry troopers in the English Civil War
an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: Veterans without a social club to join.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a society; it is a golf club, IRON, taken from Cromwell's IRONSIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Teams on opposite sides of a game are factions or bodies of people.

clue.text: Chance for commander with cowardly fellow

parts.note: OC is the military abbreviation for Officer Commanding
a cur is a contemptible, cowardly man

explanation.surface: A commanding officer gets lumbered with a coward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chance' is a verb here: to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: To chance is to happen or come about, as in 'it chanced that...'.

clue.text: In the Services he should know : the answers

definitions.text: In the Services he should know : the answers

parts.words: In the Services he should know : the answers
parts.note: Services suggests the armed forces, but means church services, where the congregation speaks set replies to the priest

explanation.surface: A military man ought to have every reply ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Services' points to the army or navy; it is church worship, where the people give the set responses.
explanation.definitionFit: One who replies, especially a worshipper speaking the set replies in a church service.

clue.text: Weller's old friend in the country

definitions.meaning: Sam Weller is the Cockney servant in Dickens's 'Pickwick Papers'
the large nation of East Asia

explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang for a mate (from china plate = mate), and the People's Republic in East Asia.

clue.text: One by one these sides appear

definitions.text: One by one these sides appear

parts.words: One by one these sides appear
parts.note: one by one written as figures is 1 1, the number of players in a cricket or football team; the sides are teams

explanation.surface: The faces of a shape emerge gradually, each in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sides' suggests faces of a shape, but means teams; '1 1' side by side reads as the number 11.
explanation.definitionFit: Football and cricket teams have eleven players each, so teams are called by that number.

clue.text: 20 ran home, having completed a circuit

definitions.meaning: the fox of 20 down fled to its burrow, its earth
electrically connected to the ground, closing the circuit

explanation.definitionFit: A fox gone to ground in its burrow, and electrical wiring connected safely to the ground.
